svg.title: Semantic scaffolding design atlas
svg.desc: Eighteen interface schematics grouped into five design families. Orange highlights each illustrated operation. These are conceptual examples, not source screenshots or quantitative marks.

text.tspan: What does the interface make possible?
Five design families · eighteen categories · 110 retained distinctions
What can a person inspect and understand?

g.title: Which aspect of the system is made inspectable?
How can a result be traced or checked?
How is content condensed, interpreted or recast?
Through which form can a person perceive meaning?

text.tspan: How can a person organise and compare material?

g.title: Which relationships give material its structure?
What is placed in a common comparison frame?
How is relevant material found and brought into view?
What is kept available for continuing the work?

text.tspan: What can a person express, change or try?

g.title: How does a person specify what the system should do?
Where can a person intervene in the work?
How are possibilities offered and shaped?
What can be tried before acting in the real setting?

text.tspan: How is the next action or reflection supported?

g.title: What helps a person decide where to look or what to do?
What basis is provided for judging the work?
What help is available, and when is it available?
How are stages, responsibilities and continuity arranged?
Which part of a person's thinking is elicited?

text.tspan: How can people share work and perspectives?

g.title: How do contributions and viewpoints become shared?
